title: Former Shelburne man dies in police custody
subtitle: None
article: A 45-year old former Shelburne man is dead, 30 hours after being Tasered by the Halifax Regional Police.

Howard Hyde made an appearance in Dartmouth Provincial Court Thursday morning, a full day after being Tasered and is believed to have died while returning to the Nova Scotia Correctional Facility in Burnside, a large facility for general population inmates.
Hyde, who suffered from schizophrenia, was shot with a Taser in the jail facility after his arrest in relation to an assault in Dartmouth just after midnight Wednesday.

Deputy Chief Tony Burbridge answered questions in a news conference Thursday. "While he was being fingerprinted," said Deputy Burbridge, "he attempted to jump over the counter in booking and flee police. The man struggled violently with our officers who tried to subdue him. They were unable to get him under control and a Taser was deployed."

Hyde continued to struggle and jumped over the counter and attempted to run out the door, claimed Deputy Burbridge. The officers pursued him and a further physical struggle ensued until he was eventually brought under control.
However, Hyde went into distress and police had to administer CPR on Hyde.
He was then transported to the hospital where he was assessed, cleared medically and released back into police custody.

By Thursday morning, Hyde had died but police are not drawing any conclusions that the Taser contributed to his death. "We need to allow the Medical Examiner time to conduct his investigation into the cause of death," explained Deputy Burbridge.
Hyde's sister Joanna Hyde received a call the morning of her brother's death from the prison chaplain.

She asked the chaplain if he had taken his medication that day but he was unable to say. "But nothing was said about a Taser. That was a big surprise to us," she said. "Its awful that my family had to be informed of this over the media."

Nova Scotia Justice Minister has ordered a ministerial review into the use of Tasers in Nova Scotia. "I have ordered Police Services officials in my department to immediately begin a review of policies and procedures regarding Taser use in Nova Scotia," said Mr. Clarke. "At the same time, RCMP are being called in to investigate the circumstances of the death at the correctional facility and I understand Halifax Regional Police will also have the RCMP conduct an external investigation into the death."
The review will examine Taser practices of authorized users in the province, including law enforcement, corrections and sheriffs.

Deputy Burbridge informed that their organization would continue to use the Taser as an option for their use of force continuum. "All medical evidence to date indicates that this tool is safe," he said.

The Hyde family was barraged with a high volume of phone calls from the media as yet another victim of Taser death was revealed. "The media response is what we have to deal with on a day I thought I was going to be grieving along with my family," said Joanna.
This incident is one of a string of recent events that have been highlighted in the media throughout the country.
Three other Canadians in the last month all died shortly after being Tasered by police including Quilem Reistre from Montreal, Robert Dziekanski from Vancouver and Claudiao Castagnetta, from Quebec.
